passage: On Friday evening the community centre's common room buzzed with Telugu, steam from the biryani and a cricket match on the wall screen. Akash stood in the doorway with his rucksack still on. "Come in, come in!" Jahnavi, the society's secretary, pulled out a chair. "First month is always the hardest." Within ten minutes somebody had asked which town he was from, somebody else had passed him a plate, and his shoulders finally dropped for the first time since the flight. He felt safe. On the walk home he thought, I could spend every evening here and never learn how to buy a bus pass. So on Monday he said yes to his lab partner's invitation to the chemistry club, and the next month he brought her to the society's dinner.

How did Akash feel after ten minutes in the common room?
qa.a: Safe and relaxed, as his shoulders dropped for the first time since the flight.

qa.a: He also said yes to the chemistry club and later brought his lab partner to the society dinner.

qa.a: As a newcomer in his hardest first month who needs a warm welcome, since Jahnavi pulled out a chair for him.

grounding: Others from the protagonist's home community welcome him warmly and he feels safe, while he also builds friendships beyond it.

passage:
International office coordinator's note, Munich.

Yamini arrived in October, pale and quiet, and missed two orientation sessions. In November the Telugu students' association invited her to their Diwali dinner. The change was visible. She began attending events, sitting with them in the canteen, laughing again. She told me, "With them I feel safe. I can just be myself."

In January I noticed something else. At a mixed group project, she sat only with the two Telugu students and didn't speak to the German and Brazilian members. One of them came to me, confused, asking if Yamini disliked them.

I mentioned it to Yamini gently. She was surprised, then thoughtful. "I didn't mean to shut them out. It's just easier."

We agreed she would join the language tandem programme alongside the association. Last week she and a German student shared lunch. She still goes to every association dinner.

- Usha

qa.q: Where did Yamini sit during the mixed group project?
qa.a: Yamini sat only with the two Telugu students.

qa.q: How did Yamini feel after joining the Telugu students' association?
qa.a: Yamini felt safe and at ease, able to be herself and laughing again.

qa.q: What balance did Usha help Yamini find?
qa.a: Usha helped Yamini keep the comfort of the association while joining the language tandem programme to make friends beyond it.

qa.q: How might the German and Brazilian group members have felt?
qa.a: They may have felt shut out and confused, wondering if Yamini disliked them.

grounding: The coordinator's note shows a young woman who feels safe in a compatriot group, learning to also make friends beyond it rather than shutting others out.

passage:
Saturday, London

The Indian society threw a welcome party tonight and I've never felt so relieved. Someone gave me rajma chawal on a paper plate. Three people spoke Hindi. A girl from Lucknow offered to show me the cheap market on Monday. I'm Ira, and I've been lonely for six weeks, and tonight I felt safe.

But something bothered me. When a British guy from my course came to say hello, a couple of the seniors laughed after he left, calling locals "cold" and "fake". Everyone nodded. I nodded too.

He'd lent me his notes last week. He's not cold.

So here's my plan. I'll go to the Indian society every Friday, happily. And I'll also say yes to his study group on Wednesday. I don't want to find family here and then be suspicious of everyone else.

qa.q: What food did someone give Ira at the party?
qa.a: Someone gave Ira rajma chawal on a paper plate.

qa.q: How did Ira feel at the welcome party?
qa.a: Ira felt relieved and safe after six lonely weeks.

qa.q: What balanced plan does Ira make?
qa.a: Ira will keep going to the Indian society every Friday but also join the British classmate's Wednesday study group, avoiding suspicion of outsiders.

qa.q: How might the British classmate have felt if Ira had joined in calling locals fake?
qa.a: He might have felt hurt and excluded, since he had been kind enough to lend his notes.

grounding: The diary shows a young person who finds warmth in a compatriot group while choosing to keep making friends beyond it and not treat outsiders with suspicion.
